newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah adjusts to central bank fixing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah adjusts to central bank fixing.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah adjusted slightly down against the dollar in slow late trading on Wednesday after the central bank raised its fixing, dealers said.
The central bank raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,331/2,523 and the conversion rate to 2,331/2,379.
One local bank dealer said the move indicated the central bank wanted to maintain a weekly three-point depreciation it has maintained over the past three weeks.
"The dollar-rupiah equilibrium seems to be at the lower end of the central bank band. It is where the fixing is," he said.
Dealers said the central bank might have absorbed some dollars from the market but probably not as much as Tuesday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,330.90/31.10 at 0945 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,330.0/31.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,330.25/30.75 and 2,329.0/29.5, respectively.
Dealers said sentiment on the rupiah remained firm and players seemed to ignore the re-election of President Clinton.
"We don't have much to do with Clinton unless something drastic happens. People here are looking at liquidity supply on Thursday and central bank fixing," a dealer said.
Dealers said operators were worried over possible implications from the last day of the Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) share offer. BNI ends its public offering on Thursday.
"We haven't seen any signs of tightening yet. Tom/next swap remains stable," one said, adding that people had factored in a flush supply due to central bank dollar buying on Tuesday.
Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 0.35/0.40.
The dealer said swap rates remained soft in slow trading.
One-month swap was at 15.5/16.5, two at 32.00/33.50, three at 50.5/52.0 and six at 96.0/97.5 points.
